prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1240; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the claimant reported a low-speed head-on collision at a residential intersection. The claimant is not represented by an attorney and gave a verbal account by phone.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and the photos taken at the scene. The report confirms the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time of the collision, and the other driver's statement matches the claimant's description of how the impact occurred.

Entry 3: Spoke with two independent witnesses who saw the collision. Both describe the same sequence of events, and neither reported any unusual behavior by either driver.

Entry 4: Inspected the vehicle. The front-end damage is consistent with the impact described and with the photos taken at the scene. No prior damage to the vehicle is recorded in the file.

Entry 5: The claimant reported shoulder pain and was evaluated at an urgent care facility. The reported injury is plausible for a collision of this type, and no prior injury to the same area is known from the claimant's history or medical records obtained so far.

Entry 6: Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy and medication. The claimant's notes show steady improvement, and the frequency of visits has tapered as the claimant's range of motion has returned.

Entry 7: A neighbor contacted the office and said the vehicle looked damaged a few weeks before the reported collision. The neighbor's recollection is unverified and has not been matched to any record, so I am following up with the claimant and the repair shop for prior service history.

Entry 8: The claimant has given the same account of the collision in every conversation so far. The driver is named on the policy, and the claim remains open pending receipt of the remaining repair and treatment records.
